claims.claim: Reviewers report that the tutorial is poorly designed, glosses over important mechanics like resources and unity, and features voice narration that interrupts itself or repeats unnecessarily.

citations.review_text: I don't think I have seen a tutorial for a game this bad, if you're going to make a complicated game, you need a good tutorial, I have seen better tutorials for Roblox games.

TLDR:
I don't know what I'm doing in this game half the time, and the tutorial is straight cheeks.

I'm playing Stellaris during the free to play weekend because it seemed interesting to me. I like space, I like management games. I decided to go with the full tutorial, and I guess I expected something way different. I was expecting it to walk me through each and every little thing that will make you successful in this game, but instead it just glosses over important things, such as resources and especially Unity. I played this ♥♥♥♥ for an hour, and I still have no idea on how to get more unity. Hovering over it with my cursor doesn't really tell me anything of value, as I don't know how to do most of the things (like improving faction approval) that increases unity. It seems to just go up and down at times with no rhyme or reason.

Another extremely annoying thing about the tutorial is that it has no priority system, or it's very poor quality. What I mean is that before I get to finish reading something, it will automatically start playing another voice clip to a completely different section unrelated to what I was currently reading. This was especially annoying at the start of the game when I was completely fresh. I would click on one thing while still reading what it would do, and then the tutorial would suddenly jump to something 5 steps ahead.

I managed to figure out how the science ships work, so I started expanding my territory with outposts, and I even started a new colony on a planet I probably shouldn't have, but whatever. I had zero clue on what any of the buildings did, but I knew I needed food, so I built more agriculture districts. Of course that didn't do anything, and I still had a food deficit. During this time, I was also coming into contact with other alien races, four of them. Four different ones. This is where it started to get really overwhelming. Every other event that was happening was trying to talk to these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and it just got really a…

Tutorial sucks, played on the free weekend, the voice narration doesn't read all the steps, and the tutorials for some repeat, even after you've already done the task, which makes you listen to the voice narration read it's short winded description yet again for the step you just did.

claims.claim: This cohort reports excessive data collection and telemetry without an easy opt-out option.

citations.review_text: No opt out for data collection. Launcher. No

[h1]I'm writing to express my concern regarding the extent of data collection in Stellaris.[/h1]

I recently learned that the game collects detailed information such as SteamID, computer configuration, gameplay behavior, progress, browser type, and IP address. This data is gathered periodically. 

I find this level of data collection excessive and intrusive. While I understand that some telemetry may support game updates and technical improvements, the scope and mandatory nature of this tracking make me uncomfortable. I did not consent to this surveillance knowingly, and I believe players should have full transparency and control over what data is collected - And the ability to opt out entirely.

As a result of these practices, I no longer wish to play Stellaris. The lack of privacy AND TRANSPARENCY, BEFORE BUYING, undermines my trust in your products. I request that you:

[b]Make data collection fully optional and opt-in.[/b] 
[b]Provide clearer disclosures BEFORE PURCHASE + installation.[/b] 
[b]And allow players to use the game without mandatory telemetry.[/b] 
I urge you to reconsider your data policies to better respect user privacy.

[h2]CLARIFYING EDIT + COMMENT RESPONSE:[/h2]

You're right. Data harvesting isn't new. But the context has drastically changed. Dismissing this as a 'ToS dive' ignores three critical shifts:

[h3]1.) The Legal Landscape (GDPR):[/h3] 

Ten+ years ago, 'IMPLICIT CONSENT' buried in a EULA was standard.
Today, under GDPR (which Paradox is legally bound by), 
consent must be FREELY GIVEN, SPECIFIC + INFORMED.

Forcing users to accept broad data harvesting just to launch a single-player game without a granular opt-out for non-essential telemetry is widely considered NON-COMPLIANT.
The issue isn't that they collect data; it's that they REMOVE USER AGENCY to refuse it while still accessing the product they bought.

[h3]2.) The Nature of the 'Partners':[/h3]

While the practice is old, the danger of the recipients has escalated. 
Paradox's…

citations.review_text:
Theres a whole lot of negatives and a few positives that shine almost so brightly that it barely overlaps some of the negatives here. So ill be listing them for easier read. Final Score at the bottom.

Positives:
- The complexity is just about right, only took me 4 hours to get a hold of the basics and some advanced stuff.
- The customization is quite good, for a space game this is exactly what you want.
- The systems are extremely good and overall cant complain when even 13 hours in im still learning.
- The Depth goes pretty far, so far in fact that you have missions for small tunnels inside small individual planets.

Negatives:
- The music, HORRID, its bleeding to the ears and torture. All i heard the entire time i was playing was '' BUM BUM BUM BUM BUM BUM BUM BUM BUM '' like jesus christ am i held up chained to a radiator in some guys basement forced to listen to the same song for 10 hours or what the heck is goin on here. 

- The extreme lack of a tutorial, although there is one it only scratches 1% of the entire systems. 99% of the things i learned i had to sit back, think for 5 minutes on why something was happening and then ultimately be forced to look it up elsewhere. 

- The overpowered AI, the first 5 hours my neighbor had amassed 10 thousand fleets and i had 1 fleet with Bob waving his hand out of the window. I was playing on normal difficulty, mind you, and by the time i had a mere 5 planets under my belt my neighbor had 50 and on top of that some guy who doesnt have a claim on anything just can roam around the map and just freely choose to just conquer your territory no problem and you cant do anything about it. Who the heck made this system????

- The hard cap on resources for no reason thus forcing the player character to be NERFED even more than they already are against these god-like AI players. It seems like the AI is just put on free no limit systems and the player is hardcapped to be stuck in the stone age. 

- Glitches are everywhere, at one po…
The learning curve is ridiculous. A lot of unnecessary BS to colonize planets and the tutorial sucks.

Stellaris is a great game for people who enjoy grand strategy, base building, and empire management. I also like that it offers so many different species and civilizations to choose from, making each playthrough feel a little different.

However, the biggest downside is the tutorial 👎. During the first hour, you're mostly reading pop-up messages explaining what different things are, but not why they matter or how to actually use them. I struggled to create a second fleet, and I couldn't understand why I wasn't able to rename it or assign a commander. In the end, ChatGPT explained that the fleet needs to contain at least one ship before you can do that. The tutorial never makes this clear.

I also couldn't understand the difference between a Defense Platform and a Corvette, or where each one is supposed to be built. Again, the tutorial doesn't explain it at all.

There is another small but annoying UI issue. In the notification settings, if you want every notification to pause the game and appear in the middle of the screen instead of disappearing as a small pop-up, you have to change every single notification... manually 😩. Why isn't there a simple "Select All" option?

Overall, I recommend the game 👍. Just be prepared for a lot of reading at the beginning... and don't be afraid to keep ChatGPT open and send it screenshots. It explained things much better than the tutorial did 🤷‍♀️.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a large amount of paid downloadable content and subscription options.

citations.review_text:
It's an interesting game stuck behind devs that are money hungry for more money and not adding enough to the base game as needed: 

I've played the game over the years and by far it's an interesting game, a perfect space RTS game that is sadly stuck behind devs who are money hungry, I understand that devs need to make money long-term but I still say to this day if it's unpopular opinion. If you're going to support the game long-term offer a season pass that lasts until the devs stop supporting the base game. Adding a subscription service is by the most scummy thing a dev can offer and it should not be supported in any mean. 

Overall the game is very interesting but it does take time to get used to it and understand and offers many hours but again the downfall this game has is the massive amounts of paid DLC that this game has most of which feels like it could be a content update for the base game. 

Performance is alright, it works with most modern PCs and I have no problem running it. 

Look the only reason I'm not going to recommended it is not because it's a bad game, no it's a very good game that offers substance on the gameplay you create but again it's stuck behind devs who are sadly money hungry. 

I would 100% recommend the game only if its on a massive deep sale, and if you are going to get the DLC & I know I'm going to sound hypocritical get one month of the subscription and try them out to determine which one is going to offer YOU gameplay. Because having to spend $248.71 to get the entire collection is ridiculous.
Single player game asking for 10€/month subscription.... Yeah, nah. They could just release the DLCs as part of the game and have happy players.

You may also be a masochist.
Best game in the galaxy. Get it, and you will understand.

Only a few hours played so far. I will certainly update my review later on. Starting this game is overwhelming. It lacks a proper tutorial but that was expected with the amount of in game systems. Lots of reading and videos watched. 
As I cannot fully review this game yet, I will still give it a thumbs up for the it's quality. It is a quality product. The support it still receives 10 years after release is also incredible. The way they handle DLCs is questionable but it isn't mandatory. You can learn the base game and slowly buy the DLCs you want to customize your experience.

EDIT: 25 hours in, this game is such a gem. I avoided Stellaris in the past because I felt intimidated by the learning curve. I spent a few hours reading about in game systems and watched a few tutorial videos and it was 100% worth it.

I am still pretty new here, especially in terms of this game and it's extremely detailed and expansive content. I am on my first playthrough and I feel like I've already got my money's worth. I am a big fan of civilization games and this plays similar to that for me, but I absolutely love the space setting and the technology aspect. Not to mention same type of deal that it feels like you can win multiple ways. I would say learning curve and difficulty are definitely harder than civilization... Which isn't a bad thing.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from excessively long loading times regardless of save age.

citations.review_text: A great system management game. I don't play it too often, but I do find myself coming back to it every once in a while and playing for days. The game is extremely complicated, and I wouldn't say this is the first management game you should play. If you have enough experience, you can find tons of systems and menus placed throughout the game, all of which serve an actual purpose in the game instead of just being fillers. if you are good at playing games with tons of systems that all manage a civilization, this is probably going to be the perfect game for you. If you want something with less systems and less complexity, I would say you might want to look at Cities: Skylines 1 or 2 (same developer) or civilization. My only complaint for this game is really just the loading times. It doesn't really seem to matter how new or old the save is (even if it's a fresh new game), the game takes forever to load. So, don't block out 15 minutes and expect to play because 10 of those might be spent loading.

My PC is the biggest pile of garbage ever, but the game manages to run okay-ish. That's all I can ask for out of a game with such depth. I haven't played in a long time, so just imagine I made this review last year.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players grapple with severe late-game lag, expensive monetization models, and ongoing multiplayer instability, even as complex menus remain rewarding.

claims.claim: Multiplayer matches suffer from persistent desync issues and stability problems that make sessions unplayable or cause them to break down across updates.

citations.review_text:
Absolutely love this game. We try playing it every week.

Emphasis on "try", because every couple of versions they break multiplayer so completely our weekly game breaks down.

It's been years of this now. STAHP.

Multiplayer is permanently broken since version 4... we play once a week for 2 hours. If you don't get screwed over by a new patch version and people wanting to restart, you get screwed by the game going into a broken state once it's run for too long (rarely even get to endgame without some catastrophe like slowdown or stutter). Every time we think this is going to be one. Every time we end up abandoning due to things breaking...

I only have this to play multiplayer, so without that it's a bust for me, can't recommend unless this gets fixed and stays fixed for a change...

If you are thinking of playing this in Multiplayer with your friends: Don't.

No matter how many times Paradox claimed to have fixed the desyncs, they never actually did. You may get lucky or you may end up with a game that is umplayable because it desyncs every 30 seconds and there is literally nothing you can do.

If you don't care about multiplayer, the game is great.

Stellaris is a game that I love playing, however that is no longer the case. DLC has ruined this game from both a price and gameplay perspective. Many of the new DLC just add two to three origins a few civics and traits, maybe a new species pack, and a shipset, so in terms of gameplay and mechanics nothing "new" is added. Instead whatever new specific mechanics, civics... etc. from the new DLC upend balance or greatly alter existing mechanics. The first case where this was change was very aparent was from the transition from Overlord -> Toxiods -> First Contact -> Galactic Paragons. Last season 9 and now season 10 are expensive and don't reveal the content you may get a blind box if you will. You might like the first DLC and decide to buy the pass only to end up with a DLC you didn't like. Overall a prices of DLC expansions has increase by around 50% and the amount of content relased durning that time is either lack luster or game breaking. Each Stellaris major version update changes and breaks the game from 2.0 to 3.0 and 3.0 to 4.0 saw significat changes in systems, mechanics, and gameplay, often being unplayable. Though I don't play a lot of multiplayer, many desync issues still persist after 4.0. In recent DLC AI dislcamers are being used, to not be speculative I wonder what other use cases is AI being used in development. If you didn't know there is (was?) a team that went back and fixed old issues and updated things to match with new DLC. But with all this new DLC, updates, and balancing, things are left behind either broken, forgotten, or become practically useless (case in point espinoge).

I have loved and played Stellaris for a very long time but this constant DLC release, ever increasing content, releasing broken features, FOMO of trying new mechancis before getting nerfed to oblivian, and content bloat. The only time I may consider buying DLC is when it's 50% in a few years. Devs fix your game is a common saying but here it really applys all the systems …

A game I would normally celebrate absolutely tarnished by overpriced DLC and desyncs that haven't been fixed for what feels like years.

I had hoped more people in the community would see this for what it is; unacceptable. 

I suppose this review is largely moot if you intend to never play with a friend, but if you do, give it a wide berth.
multiplayer with friends has turned into a frustrating experience of hoping the game can recover from desyncs.
i love this game but **** what the **** is wrong with paradox why are you still dropping dlc bull**** when your ******* multiplayer doesn't  even work either fix it or drop a new  stellaris

[h1]Gameplay Experience:[/h1]
This is one of the most chill games. Every time I start it anew it fills me with beauty and wonder. The quest blurbs are actually intriguing; not just obtrusive massive walls of text. I love exploring and running into life and ancient ruins of old civilizations throughout the cosmos. 
The combat is fairly automatic. Fights are mostly decided through preparation and strategy (some weapons and armor are better for different opposition for example).
Only good things to say about the general game design.

[h3]Gameplay nitpick:[/h3]
It's kind of an annoyance that they keep updating and changing the game years after it should have been finalized. Some functions we had - like the ability to set fleets to patrol a route - don't exist at all anymore. Honestly making a review for this game requires me not to specify anything too thoroughly because they change things. A year from now it might not have the thing I mention.

[h1]Financial Experience:[/h1]
At first I thought it'd be "A" dlc. Then they came out with another that I grabbed. If I'm honest at this point I just feel to committed to care about "one more purchase". But if I were to approach this game today and see this lineup of DLCs needed I wouldn't even touch it.

[h1]Technical Experience:[/h1]
For a [u]2016[/u] game it's pretty heavy. It's fast early-game but no matter what speed setting you have on it'll always be a crawl by the endgame.
Stability varies on a day-by-day basis. One day it can be working fine. Next day it has a 2-second delay and a memory leak that it'll have to fix on its own before it's good again.

claims.claim: The game features an extremely steep learning curve with complex menus and deep systems that can be overwhelming to new players.

citations.review_text: This game is deep, intricate, and requires investment to get the best value out of it. That said, it is quite fun and I do not regret any of the money I have spent on the original game or dlc's.

You'll spend more time making your character/empire and lore building than playing the actual game. Which is great, also this game goes from a 8/10 to a 11/10 if you play with real people or have all the DLC. Also the monthly subscription will do you good for a long bit if you just get the 6 month option. Be prepared to use your brain a lot tho, your managing a galaxy spanning empire after all.

Woof, holy STEEP learning curve. If this is your first "menu game", stop. Do not pass go. Do not collect the video game. Start somewhere else. Pick something easier and then come back to this after minimum 6 months. Even if you have someone to explain it to you and answer all your questions, it's rough. There are menus I have barely even managed to start looking at in the games i have played due to the sheer amount of ♥♥♥♥ you need to be doing at all times, while also having plot/event menus pop up that you have to try to half-read. There is so much stuff that the tutorial doesn't even begin to touch on that I look at and am like "i literally don't even know where to begin with that". I've found myself in a "kinda love it, kinda hate it" relationship with this game. Few games give me a headache after playing like this one does. The nail in the coffin though is the DLC price. Insanity.
The very best 4x game in existence. Do you need a college degree to play it? Yes. But it's worth it.

[h1]A Universe Limited Only by Your Imagination[/h1]

There are very few strategy games that give you the amount of freedom Stellaris does.

Before you even unpause the game, you've already created your own civilization. You decide your species, ethics, government, origin, traits, ship designs, and more. Whether you want to be a peaceful federation, a ruthless machine intelligence, a devouring hive mind, or a fanatical empire bent on galactic conquest, Stellaris lets you tell your own story.

That sense of customization and roleplaying is easily one of the game's greatest strengths.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Exploration Done Right[/h2]

The early game is where Stellaris truly shines.

Exploring unknown star systems, uncovering ancient civilizations, making first contact with alien empires, and discovering strange anomalies constantly gives you something to look forward to. It captures the excitement of exploring a galaxy better than almost any game I've played.

Every campaign feels like the beginning of a new science fiction story.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]A Game of Incredible Depth[/h2]

That same depth is also what makes Stellaris difficult to recommend.

With hundreds of hours played, I still don't feel like I fully understand all of its mechanics. Economy, trade, diplomacy, planet specialization, fleet design, ascension paths, population management... there's always another system to learn.

For some players, that's exactly what makes Stellaris so rewarding.

For others, it'll be overwhelming.

Neither is wrong.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The DLC Problem[/h2]

My biggest criticism isn't the complexity—it's the amount of DLC.

Paradox has supported Stellaris for years, and that's helped the game grow into something truly impressive. Unfortunately, it also means many mechanics and playstyles are spread across a long list of expansions.

As a new player, it can feel less like you're buying a complete game and more like you're trying to figure out which DLC contains the features everyone else i…

This is a very complicated strategy game with a lot of depth. You will lose slowly and painfully over and over as you try to figure things out. There's nothing wrong with that if that's your cup of tea.

What's wrong with the game is that the Devs won't leave it the eff alone. DLC and expansions are great...but not if they rewrite the fundamental mechanics every time they want to introduce something new. I was never great at this game, but I could hold my own after a month or so of experimenting. After 100 hours in game, I can no longer play the game that I bought, and the dozens of changes are so disorienting I can't get any traction no matter what I do.

In short, I can't recommend this game unless it's going to be THE GAME you play for a while. If you're dedicated enough to keep up with the changes and master and re-master the systems, there's a lot to play with in here. Most of it's buried under layers of tedious complexity, but some people like that. I have no idea whether the devs are done mucking around, it's been years and they keep doing things to the game.

claims.claim: The monetization model relies on an extensive and costly collection of downloadable content expansions alongside a subscription option.

citations.review_text:
Stellaris is a game that has changed a lot over the years, with the way planets, governments, and just about everything besides the rough outline of fleet combat being unrecognizable from release. Having played quite a bit of the game through multiple eras, I can safely say I approve of the vast majority of these changes; the game is much better now than it is on release, but I can understand how this ship of theseus style of game design can be alienating to other veterans. I'll also concede that there's a great deal of bugs floating around, some are indeed game breaking/run ending, but most are a nuisance at worst. The absolute worst thing I can say about the game is that the pricetag on the entire collection of DLCs is so prohibitive that unless you've been keeping up from the beginning, your best bet for affording the full experience is to pay the subscription fee for full access.

All that said, I think this is the single best Space Empire 4X game there is, absolutely no competition. If you can stomach the negatives, it's everything you'd be looking for in the genre.

But there are a lot of them, and because they're so content heavy, the base game seems so small without them. It's totally not the case btw, the base game is still really good, the dlcs are just that good, also my reccomendations for said dlcs 

Machine Age is a must if you like robots, Biogenesis is quite good, do reccomend, Lithoids is seen as bad by a lot of people but the species are just incredibly good looking, I use one of them half the time, Infernals is really good too.

Also talking about species, create or loggin into your paradox account, the behemothkin species that you get from it is like in my top five species ever, and it goes well with Biogenesis for obvious reasons (the Behemoth)

also there is a mod workshop with a lot of good things, would reccomend Gigastructural Engineering if you like huge things (attack moon go brrr) or Ancient Cashe Of Technology (ACOT) if you like small but powerful tech, and both at the same time is kinda ridiculous.

 Also the species mods by Silfae are really good, and there is two Star Trek total conversion mods, two Star Wars ones, and a Mass Effect one so a lot of potential, and the youtubers that play the game are generally really funny and the community is the opposite of toxic and kinda funny but on the good side of funny

Also you can buy a subscription to have all DLCs but i think it's gonna make the base game feel weird and empy after all and paying for a subscription every month seems like a bad idea for me but you do what you want

PS: thanks for the feedback

Like all paradox games, this is a scam meant to sell you DLC. The base game is a hollow shell. I paid for 1 month subscription to all the DLC and I can tell you that none of it is worth your cold hard cash. They sell you almost nothing in each DLC. It only looks like a lot of content spread out over 10 years of bloated development. They still demand retail prices for new DLC and season passes. The next DLC they promise ships that function like planets. Sounds cool but not worth paying money for it. If Paradox was a good company, they would have stopped developing this game and made Stellaris 2. But the quality in their games have spiraled into the gutter and all they care about is milking DLC. All the veterans are mad about changes and it's clear the game's balance is ruined with each new patch. They censor forums, ban dissenting opinions, and have armies of shills that will berate you for any criticism. Once you have played a complete game or two, everything becomes boring and the events are no longer interesting.

I loved this game at launch and for the first few DLCs but at this point I cannot in good conscience recommend anyone wastes their time and money on it.

Paradox seem determined to match the pace of releases set by Wizards of the Coast with Magic the Gathering and the constant churn of additional content.  Whilst the use of AI-generated material is also certainly a problem, it is a small point compared the colossal cost-to-benefit ratio of this game.

The base game costs £34.99 (before sales discounts, though at time of writing was reduced to £8.74).  This is already the price of a full game, and indeed many quality titles sell for less.

Then there is the mind-boggling cost of the DLC content - £300.57 (before sales discounts, though at time of writing this was only reduced to £178.22, and not including soundtrack or e-book).

To purchase the complete game at full price would be £335.56 at base cost or £186.96 at sale price at time of writing, not including the soundtrack or e-book.

Sure you could purchase the expansion pass but for all the content, you'll be locked into this game and nothing else for the next year at least if you want to get your money's worth out of it before you cancel and never play Stellaris again.  Or you'll be paying it every month forever, at which point Paradox have far exceeded the already outrageous up-front cost.

Stellaris started out as a wonderful concept, fantastically executed, but over time that shine has dimmed.  DLC has been mass-produced purely to generate additional income with little regard to quality or user experience, let alone any thought or respect given to the user's time or money.

Your time is valuable and your money is hard-earned.  This game absolutely does not respect yours, or anyone else's (including artists and creators).  In no world is £180 or more a reasonable price for a video game.  Avoid it.  It's just not worth it.

One of the most expensive games I've seen, if you actually want to fully play it.
The initial game is nice and cheap, and fun... however, if you want the full game, prepare to spend LOTS.
This is the first game I've ever seen actually allow you to RENT THE EXPANSIONS~?~?  Insane.  

Base game is fun, but over time it has bloated into such an incredible expense that I can't justify continuing with it.  They should have just made a sequel or six years ago rather than the insane number of expansions.
